findings: One-story pilot is not an enablement result: 8/81 polarity pairs disagreed (9.9%), and paired averaging raised human-rating error to 0.263 vs 0.244 positive-only, so dual polarity currently injects noise rather than cancelling bias.

Arithmetic averaging is the wrong default aggregator. Dual polarity is optional per module only when it is a proven bias correction; the pilot pattern is the signature of a noisier negated form (or misspecified scoring), not of complementary signal.
Four-state inversion is not Boolean not(). Map YES↔NO; leave NA→NA and CANNOT_ASSESS→CANNOT_ASSESS. Mixing NA/CA into 0/0.5/1 before averaging is invalid and can alone explain worse error.

Inconsistency must be typed, not collapsed: (1) polarity contradiction (YES vs NO after inversion), (2) determinate vs CANNOT_ASSESS, (3) determinate vs NA (usually a wording/applicability bug), (4) NA vs CANNOT_ASSESS (taxonomy confusion).

¬Q must be the logical dual of Q (same predicate, same scope, same NA preconditions). Rhetorical opposites, extra quantifiers (never/all/fail to), or shifted speech-acts are not duals and must not enter a reconcile path.

Repeatability interaction: if polarity-pair disagreement ≈ same-polarity test–retest disagreement, dual-asking is a second noisy draw, not acquiescence control. Averaging then reduces error only if negated variance is comparable and errors are weakly/negatively correlated; the pilot implies the opposite.

Creative-writing binaries are heterogeneous. Concrete presence items with low NA/CA can eventually justify dual polarity; subjective craft items (voice, originality, pacing) with high CA and low κ are the worst candidates because negation raises cognitive/LLM load.
Yes-bias / LLM acquiescence is a reason to test dual polarity in shadow, not a reason to enable it. Known negation-processing error can exceed the bias you hoped to cancel.
recommendations: Default dual polarity OFF globally. Production score = canonical (usually positive) polarity. Do not ship paired averaging from this pilot.

Enable module M only if all gates pass on a pre-registered holdout, not the calibration story: (E1) coverage ≥~20 stories × multiple judges/models and ≥~200 pairs for M so a 10% disagreement rate has a tight CI; (E2) primary metric dual-reconciled error < positive-only by a pre-set practical delta (must reverse 0.263 vs 0.244), 95% interval excluding 0 or meeting the delta; (E3) on the disagreement subset, dual/negated is closer to gold at least as often as positive-only—if positive wins disagreements, averaging cannot help; (E4) NA invariance ≥95% and CA invariance ≥90% under the four-state map; (E5) inter/intra-rater reliability of the dual score ≥ positive-only minus a small ε, and polarity disagreement is not fully explained by same-polarity noise; (E6) human logical-dual review of ¬Q wording; (E7) incremental cost justified (e.g. Δerror ≱ ~0.01 vs 0.244 baseline → keep OFF); (E8) two consecutive evaluation windows pass E2–E5.

Reconcile; do not mean. Policy: consistent determinate pair → that answer; polarity contradiction → prefer canonical polarity or abstain/CA/human review (choose one policy and freeze it); any NA with a determinate answer → item defect, exclude from score; CA with a determinate answer → do not average, either propagate CA or keep determinate with a flag. Never encode NA/CA as numeric midpoints unless that mapping is separately calibrated to gold.

Cost-aware sparse testing until gates pass: shadow dual-ask a stratified 10–15% of items (or boundary/low-confidence positives only); never mix shadow dual answers into production; freeze module on/off rather than item-level fishing after seeing gold; re-estimate gates after N new stories. Prefer rewriting the canonical item into the easier natural polarity over permanently asking both.

Report a 4×4 positive×negated contingency; logical-consistency rate; inconsistency-type breakdown; error for positive-only, negated-only, dual-average, and dual-reconcile; disagreement-conditional gold analysis; per-module and per-story slices; κ/ICC by polarity and mixed-polarity; extra judgments/tokens; enabled-module list with evidence version and kill rule (subsequent dual error ≥ positive-only, NA/CA leakage over threshold, or cost without maintained gain).
Use dual polarity as a diagnostic even when OFF: high polarity contradiction on an item is a prompt to revise Q/¬Q or drop the item, not to average it.
risks: Enabling from one story overfits 81 pairs and the 8 disagreements; 9.9% has a wide interval and may not replicate.
Naive averaging and NA/CA numeric encoding will keep dual polarity looking harmful even if a correct reconcile rule would help, or conversely hide item defects.
Negated wording that is not a true logical dual silently measures a different construct (stricter absence, different quantifier, moralized 'failure').
Low-repeatability subjective modules plus negation will inflate pair disagreement that looks like 'signal' and degrade both accuracy and κ.
Per-item enablement after peeking at gold, or pooling modules, will create false enables (Simpson confounding of easy vs hard items).
Doubling judge/LLM cost for a method that already lost 0.019 error vs positive-only is a poor default under any realistic accuracy-value function.
If disagreement is sent to humans without a freeze policy, dual polarity becomes an unbounded review queue rather than a scorer.
output.summary: Keep dual polarity off. The one-story pilot (8/81 = 9.9% pair disagreement; paired average error 0.263 vs 0.244 positive-only) is evidence to refuse production averaging, not to ship it. Optionally ask both polarities only per module after holdout gates show dual-reconciled error beating positive-only, disagreement that tracks gold rather than negation noise, four-state inversion with NA and CANNOT_ASSESS left unflipped, no repeatability regression, and cost worth the delta. Until then, shadow-sample 10–15%, report 4×4 consistency and disagreement-conditional error, and reconcile with a typed policy rather than a mean.
